description:
Improve your intermediate Chinese listening skills (HSK 4-5) with this natural conversation about perfectionism, procrastination, and why you should stop waiting for the perfect moment to start. This episode of "Everyday Chinese" is designed to help you understand real-world dialogue in a relaxed and engaging way.

In this video, hosts Li Ming and Wang Yu discuss the common psychological reasons we delay starting new projects, from fear of failure to "analysis paralysis." You will learn practical strategies to overcome these hurdles, such as breaking down tasks, setting up an "experiment period," and using the "five-minute rule." This is the perfect listening practice to not only boost your Mandarin fluency but also get motivated to achieve your own goals!

Timestamp:
00:00 - Intro & introducing today's topic.
02:25 - Discussing the main reasons we wait: fear of failure and perfectionism.
07:16 - Introducing the concept of "Analysis Paralysis" (分析瘫痪).
12:37 - Practical advice begins: Lower your expectations for the first step.
18:36 - Vocabulary explanation starts with "Procrastination" (拖延症).
22:52 - Final thoughts and a question for the audience.

GET THE FULL SCRIPT:
https://chinesedailypodcast.blogspot.com/2026/03/podcast-99.html

📝 Key Vocabulary from this Episode:
拖延症 (tuō yán zhèng) - Procrastination
门槛 (mén kǎn) - Threshold / barrier to entry
循序渐进 (xún xù jiàn jìn) - To proceed step by step
顾虑 (gù lǜ) - Concern / worry
分析瘫痪 (fēn xī tān huàn) - Analysis paralysis
幸存者偏差 (xìng cún zhě piān chā) - Survivorship bias
